commits.messageBody:
A reset in the middle of a read leaves the peripheral driving the byte it
was sending. release_held_sda() clocked SCL only until SDA first read high,
then sent one STOP. SDA is also high for a 1 bit of that byte, and the
peripheral takes it low again for the next 0 bit, which is the moment the
STOP needs it high. The STOP fails, the bus is reported absent and the
board is not detected.

On ToughC5 (ESP32-C5) with a UnitNFC on Port.A, resets during reads left
both lines low before detection, and every such boot came up with
getBoard() == 0x00 and no I2C at all: 16 of 94 boots on an older develop
(6f81929), 2 of 30 on develop with #423.

Try a STOP after every clock instead, until SDA stays high. The
peripheral lets go of SDA in the acknowledge slot at the latest, so a
transmitter releases within 9 clocks; one more covers a receiver holding
SDA in its own acknowledge slot.

held_sda_release.cpp drives the real function against a peripheral model
left at each low bit of the bytes the UnitNFC returns, a receiver in its
acknowledge slot, SCL held low and an idle bus. The previous code fails
its first case.

Refs #424
commits.messageHeadline: board_detect: keep clocking a held SDA until a STOP holds

title: board_detect: SDA の解放で、STOP が成立するまでクロックを出し続ける
